description: Surfaced by fz-9gp (2026-07-15). The send/2 spec is now pid | integer -- documenting actual runtime semantics (fz_send_ref takes raw u64 bits, no registry) and a corpus-wide convention (~16 fixtures: zero-capture spawned children send(1, ...) to reach main because no self()/registry/pid-threading exists for them). Elixirs contract is pid | port | registered-name, NOT arbitrary integers. DECIDE: (a) keep integer addressing as a documented fz semantic; (b) add a registry / named-process mechanism and tighten the spec to pid | name; (c) make spawn provide parent/self pids to children. Then re-pin the corpus convention accordingly. Language-design decision -- needs the user.
title: process addressing: send/2 accepts raw integer indexes because zero-capture children cannot obtain a pid -- decide the real contract
